page.layout: One page of text in a single column; at the left edge, cut-off fragments of text from the facing page (a margin block of partial words, not transcribed as notes because they are fragments of the neighbouring page's text and edge); running head at top centre; page number at top right; catchword/signature line at foot.

main_text.p: 90 Adjunctum non magis distribui potest in commune & proprium, quàm subjectum, effectum, & causa.
92 Omnis unitas & identitas rerum inter se fluit ex affectione consentanea, vel ejusdem causæ, vel ejusdem effecti, vel ejusdem subjecti, vel ejusdem adjuncti.
93 Nullæ duæ sunt res, quæ non inter se & consentiant & dissentiant.
96 Diversa generatim dicuntur, quæ non sunt eadem.
97 Speciatim diversa appellantur, quæ ita non sunt eadem, ut possint tamen aliquo modo esse eadem, id est, eidem attribui.
98 Diversa dissentiunt non tantùm ratione ratiocinante, vel conceptu nostro, sed etiam, ut loquuntur, ratione ratiocinatâ, vel ratione suâ.
99 Dissensio hæc rationis, est quod duæ res non sint causæ ejusdem effecti, vel effecta ejusdem causæ, vel subjecta ejusdem adjuncti, vel adjuncta ejusdem subjecti.
100 Omnia diversa si considerentur in natura

page.notes: Printed side-number "100" is partly obscured and read as "1oo"; the line ends at the catchword "natura". Left-edge fragments (tiam, tiam, eati, ver-, ate-, etc.) belong to the adjacent page and were not transcribed. Several words in the lines of paragraphs 92, 97, 98 and 99 are blurred by show-through and are read with some doubt.
